problem.statement: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.

prev.meaning: The head of the portion of the list whose links have already been reversed.

curr.meaning: The first node in the portion of the original list that has not yet been reversed.

next_node.meaning: The original successor of curr, saved before curr's next link is redirected.

representation_requirements.description: Represent each node with a value and one next edge, using null to mark the tail.
Represent prev, curr, and next_node as named references at each iteration.
Represent the processed prefix with reversed links and the unprocessed suffix with original links.
Represent prev as the new head when curr is null.

semantic_invariants.statement: Each node has at most one outgoing next link, and following next links from curr identifies the original unprocessed successor chain.
Before curr's next link is changed, next_node holds curr's original successor, preserving access to the unprocessed suffix.
After each completed iteration, the processed prefix is reversed and its head is prev.
At the start of each iteration, prev is the reversed processed-prefix head and curr is the first node of the unprocessed suffix.
When curr is null, all nodes have been processed and prev is the new head, or null for an empty input.

completion_evidence.description: Identifies the single next link from each node and the null-terminated tail.
Shows next_node equal to curr's original successor before any link mutation.
Demonstrates saving next_node before redirecting curr's next link to prev.
Shows prev advancing to curr and curr advancing to next_node after reversal.
Verifies that curr is null and the returned reference is prev.

terminal_behavior: Initialize prev to null and curr to the input head.
While curr is not null, save curr's original successor in next_node.
Redirect curr's next link to prev.
Advance prev to curr and curr to next_node.
When curr is null, return prev as the new head; an empty input returns null.
